Lifecycle hooks are user-supplied shell scripts that the harness runs at fixed
pipeline boundaries. Drop an executable script at
`<project>/.papercusp/hooks/<name>.sh` and the engine invokes it when the
matching event fires. The runner is `runHook()` in
`libs/papercusp/packages/orchestrator/src/hooks.ts`: it looks up
`<stateDir>/hooks/<name>.sh`, skips silently if the file is missing or not
executable (any execute bit set — `mode & 0o111`, so owner, group, **or**
other counts), runs it with `cwd` set to the project
directory, captures combined stdout+stderr to
`<stateDir>/logs/hooks/<unix-seconds>-<name>.log`, and logs a non-zero exit as
a warning — a failing hook never halts the mission. On Windows the script
needs `bash` on `PATH` (Git for Windows ships one); the desktop bootstrap
surfaces that prerequisite.

## Why hooks instead of in-prompt actions

This is design intent carried over from the first harness generation, and it
still holds: hooks are **out-of-band**. They consume no tokens, add no latency
to any LLM call, and fire **deterministically** — not "if the agent decides
to". Anything you'd otherwise bolt onto a role prompt as "and also send a
Slack message" belongs in a hook, keeping each prompt focused on the role's
one job.

## Hooks that fire today

The legacy bash run-loop fired ten hook events; that loop is retired
(`libs/papercusp/_retired/orchestrator-run-loop/`). In the current DBOS
pipeline, hooks fire from the **finalizer** — the step list that
`planFinalization()` builds when a feature pipeline ends in DONE or ESCALATE
(`packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/orchestrator-finalize.ts`). Two hook names
are wired:

| Hook | Fires | Event-specific env | Call site |
|---|---|---|---|
| `on-escalate` | Pipeline finalizes with **ESCALATE**, before the `onEscalate` recipe roles run | `REASON`, `PROJECT_DIR`, `STATE_DIR` | `orchestrator-runner.ts:930` |
| `afterDone` | Pipeline finalizes **DONE** (and the done-gates pass), after the `onDone` recipe roles run | `TRIGGER=done`, `FEATURE_ID`, `PROJECT_DIR`, `STATE_DIR` | `orchestrator-runner.ts:952` |

A blocked DONE skips the whole finalization step list, hook included.
`planFinalization()` blocks completion on **any** of three conditions: an open
needs-human plan item, a configured smoke gate that ran and failed
(`smokeEnabled && smokePassed === false`), or — for a `human-gate` acceptance
blueprint — an approval that hasn't been granted yet
(`acceptanceKind === 'human-gate' && !acceptanceApproved`). Any of these and
the `afterDone` hook never runs.

The roles that surround the hooks are **declarative**, not hardcoded:
`planFinalization()` resolves the finalize recipe from the harness's
`.papercusp/blueprint.yaml` `gates.finalize`, defaulting to the coding
blueprint's recipe (`onDone`: curator → postCuratorOutputs → documenter →
`[archive]`; `onEscalate`: curator). A non-coding POT blueprint can override
`gates.finalize`, so the hooks fire around whatever finalize recipe that
harness declares. A `judge`-acceptance blueprint additionally inserts a
`judge`-role acceptance gate before the `onDone` recipe whose `revise` verdict
hard-blocks the **rest** of the finalize recipe: the runner `break`s out of the
finalize step loop, so every remaining step — including the `afterDone` hook,
which the finalizer appends last — is skipped. `afterDone` fires only on a
normal accepted `DONE` finalize.

`runHook()` itself accepts any name — the engine isn't limited to these two —
but no other call site exists in the live tree, so no other event fires. The
pre/post-worker, validator, smoke, checkpoint and competition hooks from the
bash era retired with the run-loop.

### The `afterDone` builtin

`afterDone` has a TS builtin behind it: when **no** user hook script ran, the
finalizer calls `notifyParentOnDone()`
(`packages/operator-core/lib/dbos/notify-parent-done.ts`), which posts a
`Completion` message to this harness's parent — so a parent that spawned this
harness as a child learns the sub-work is done. The parent slug is read from PG
(`harness_shared.projects.parent_slug`, sealed server-side at scaffold time by
`doScaffoldHarness`), **not** from config. The message fires **only when the
harness's feature queue has fully drained** — every other feature is `passed`
or `deprecated`, excluding the feature that triggered this finalize. A
non-drained queue is a **silent no-op**: the builtin returns a typed reason
(`no_parent` / `queue_not_drained` / `send_failed` / `lookup_failed`) and posts
nothing. A per-harness `hooks/afterDone.sh` **overrides the builtin entirely**
(parity with the retired bash builtin resolver). Plugin hooks fire regardless
(below).

## Environment a hook receives

On top of the event-specific variables in the table, `runHook()` auto-injects
context so scripts can query the operator instead of scraping harness files
(`hooks.ts:105–113`):

- `HARNESS_SLUG` — the current harness slug (defaults to the project
  directory's basename when not passed explicitly)
- `WORKSPACE_ID` — the active workspace, when known
- `OPERATOR_BASE` — operator API base URL; defaults to
  `$PAPERCUSP_OPERATOR_BASE`, then `http://localhost:3070` (the operator API
  port — `:3055` is the Vite content port with no `/api` routes, the EI-113
  wrong-stack default that audit P-038 fixed)

The full process environment is inherited too; the caller's explicit env wins
over the injected values on conflict.

**Hooks must not read harness state from the filesystem.** Files like
`lanes.json` no longer exist at runtime — PG is the runtime store-of-record
(see [Storage policy](/internal/docs/system/storage-policy)). The contract in
`hooks.ts` is: query the operator API instead.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Example: .papercusp/hooks/afterDone.sh — look up feature state via the API
features=$(curl -fsS "$OPERATOR_BASE/api/harness/$HARNESS_SLUG/features")
status=$(echo "$features" | jq -r '.[] | select(.id == "'"$FEATURE_ID"'") | .status')
```

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Example: .papercusp/hooks/on-escalate.sh — page a Slack channel
curl -X POST -H 'Content-type: application/json' \
  --data "{\"text\":\"Mission escalated: $REASON\"}" \
  "$SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL"
```

Make scripts executable (`chmod +x`) — a non-executable file is skipped
without error.

## Plugin hooks fire alongside

User hook scripts are per-harness; **plugins** hook the same lifecycle
globally. At the `afterDone` step the finalizer fires the in-process typed
hook `firePluginLifecycle('afterDone', …)` on every loaded plugin that
declares a handler (one of the FROZEN legacy fire-points —
plugin-system-pot-port D-003), then emits the `pipeline:done:<slug>:<feature>`
event. Plugin hook failures are logged by the host and ignored; plugin hooks
fire whether or not a user hook script ran. (The old per-plugin shell-out via
the `papercusp-fire-hook` CLI was retired 2026-06-12 — plugin-system-pot-port
P-006.) New pipeline integrations should not use typed hooks at all: declare
**event-reaction rules** on the pipeline event vocabulary instead — see
[Plugins](/internal/docs/spec/plugins).

## Managing hook scripts over the API

`packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/harness/hooks.ts` exposes
CRUD for hook scripts: `GET /api/harness/:slug/hooks` (list known hooks with
content + executable bit), `PUT`/`DELETE /api/harness/:slug/hooks/:name`
(write with `chmod 755` / remove), and
`GET /api/harness/:slug/hook-logs/:logId` to read a hook-run log. The
`hooks:known` tool returns the same name list.

The known-hooks list comes from `getKnownHooks()`
(`packages/operator-core/lib/known-hooks.ts`), which returns the `live` rows of
a static `DBOS_PIPELINE_HOOKS` registry — yielding `['afterDone',
'on-escalate']` (sorted). So the API lists, and accepts writes to,
`afterDone`/`on-escalate` (the two that fire) and **rejects** names that aren't
live, such as the bash-era `pre-worker` (catalogued `status: 'lost'`, not
returned). A drift guard (`known-hooks.test.ts`) greps the live firing sites
under `lib/dbos/` and asserts set equality with the registry's `live` rows, so
adding a `runHook(...)` call without a registry row fails the build.
`runHook()` itself never consults this list, so scripts created directly on
disk run regardless of whether the API would have allowed the name.

(Earlier the registry was instead derived by grepping the now-retired
`main-loop.ts`, which always found nothing and fell back to `['pre-worker']` —
advertising a hook that never fires and hiding the two that do. The static
registry replaced that grep in `papercusp-full-app-audit-2026-06-09` P-016
(EI-94).)
